However, the industry extends far beyond the cockpit, with opportunities for graduates of several other disciplines.
From designing and maintaining an aircraft, monitoring weather conditions and ensuring aviation safety, the industry depends on professionals with diverse academic backgrounds.
As such, prospective university students may consider several courses to get into the different sectors of the industry.
Below are some courses you can study to get into the aviation industry in Nigeria.
Aeronautical Engineering focuses on the design, development, testing and maintenance of aircraft, including their structures, engines and flight systems.
The course provides students with knowledge of aerodynamics, aircraft propulsion, flight mechanics and aviation technology.
Graduates can pursue careers in aircraft engineering, research and development, aircraft design and maintenance, subject to the relevant professional licensing requirements.
Universities offering these courses include Air Force Institute of Technology (AFIT), Obafemi Awolowo University, University of Uyo, and the likes.
Mechanical Engineering deals with the design, manufacture, operation and maintenance of mechanical systems.
In aviation, the discipline is relevant to aircraft engines, propulsion systems, mechanical components and maintenance operations.
Graduates can work in aircraft maintenance organisations, engineering departments, technical operations and aviation equipment manufacturing, although some positions require additional professional qualifications.
Some Universities offering these courses include University of Lagos, Obafemi Awolowo University, University of Nigeria, Nsukka, University of Uyo, and Lagos State University of Science and Technology.
Hospitality and Tourism Management focuses on customer service, tourism operations, accommodation management and the organisation of travel-related services.
The course is relevant to aviation because airlines and airports require professionals who can manage passenger experiences, customer relations and hospitality services.
Graduates can explore careers in airline customer service, airport hospitality, passenger relations, tourism management and travel services.
Universities offering this course include Lagos State University of Science and Technology, Elizade University, and Trinity University.
Mass Communication involves the study of journalism, public relations, broadcasting, advertising and strategic communication.
Within the aviation industry, communication professionals help airlines, airports and regulatory agencies manage their public image, communicate with passengers and maintain relationships with the media.
Graduates can work as aviation journalists, flight attendants, public relations officers, corporate communication specialists, media relations officers and content managers.
So many universities in Nigeria offer this course, including University of Lagos, University of Nigeria, Nsukka, Federal University Lokoja, and University of Ilorin.
Computer Science focuses on computer systems, programming, and software development.
The aviation industry relies on technologies for passenger information systems, airline websites, flight bookings, baggage handling, flight scheduling, aircraft monitoring and cybersecurity.
Graduates can pursue a career in aviation technology, software development, data analysis, information systems management and cybersecurity.
For prospective university students, Obafemi Awolowo University, University of Nigeria, Nsukka, University of Aeronautics and Aerospace Engineering, and Al-Hikmah University, Ilorin are some universities offering this course.
Civil Engineering deals with the planning, design, construction and maintenance of infrastructure.
In aviation, civil engineers contribute to airport development, including the construction and maintenance of runways, taxiways, terminals, drainage systems and other airport facilities.
Graduates can work in airport infrastructure development, construction management, engineering consultancy and facilities maintenance.
Some universities worth checking out include Federal University of Transportation, Daura, Elizade University, Obafemi Awolowo University, and others.
These three disciplines provide opportunities for individuals interested in the commercial and financial aspects of aviation.
Business Administration focuses on business operations, management, organisational planning and administration. Graduates can work in airline management, airport administration, human resources and business development.
Accounting involves financial reporting, auditing, budgeting and financial management. Graduates can work in the finance departments of airlines, airports and aviation organisations.
Economics examines markets, financial systems, resource allocation and economic policies. In aviation, graduates can work in industry research, economic planning, market analysis and aviation policy.
Universities offering these courses include University of Lagos, University of Nigeria, Nsukka, Federal University Lokoja, etc.
Law is another academic discipline that can lead to opportunities in the aviation industry.
The sector operates under national and international legal frameworks covering aircraft operations, aviation safety, passenger rights, commercial agreements and regulatory compliance.
Law graduates can specialise in aviation law and work with airlines, airports, aviation regulatory agencies and other organisations.
Potential career paths include aviation lawyers, legal advisers, regulatory compliance officers and aviation policy specialists.
Universities like Baze University, Alhikmah University, University of Ilorin, and others currently offer this course.
Aviation and Transport Management is one of the most directly relevant courses for students interested in the business and operational aspects of the aviation industry.
The course focuses on airline operations, airport management, aviation economics, transportation systems, logistics, passenger services and aviation regulations.
Graduates can pursue careers as airport operations officers, airline administrators, aviation planners, logistics managers and transport operations specialists.
Universities offering this course include African Aviation and Aerospace University, Baze University, Federal University of Transportation, Daura, and so on.
Although these courses can provide academic foundations for careers in aviation, obtaining a university degree does not automatically qualify graduates for every position in the industry.
Certain professions, including pilots, air traffic controllers and aircraft maintenance engineers, require specialised training, professional licences and certifications.
The Nigerian Civil Aviation Authority (NCAA) regulates aviation personnel licensing and establishes the professional requirements for specific safety-related positions.
Prospective students should therefore consider the requirements of their preferred career paths and verify that their chosen university offers an appropriately accredited programme.
They should also check the current admission requirements through the Joint Admissions and Matriculation Board (JAMB) and individual university admission offices before making their choices.
Ultimately, the aviation industry offers opportunities for graduates of different academic disciplines, demonstrating that a career in the sector does not necessarily begin with studying Aeronautical Engineering or becoming a pilot.
